name: fill a large memory pseudorandomly, then read it back in a data-dependent order
mechanism: expand the input into a large array of pseudorandom blocks, then perform many rounds in which the current value selects which stored block to mix in next; computing the result without keeping the whole array forces recomputation, so the cost is memory times time and cannot be parallelised cheaply

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'scrypt' in section Computer science / Cryptography:

fails_when: data-dependent access leaks timing; the memory parameter must fit the legitimate device
